MCPHub identity spoofing — admin-themed username in /<user>/sse path AIExploitation High
High-fidelity alert for GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf exploitation: requests to MCPHub `/<user>/sse` where the user-segment matches privileged-role keywords (admin, administrator, root, sudo, owner, superuser, sysadmin, ceo, cfo, cto, operator) or the literal PoC string `CEO-admin-impersonated`. Because the segment is taken verbatim as the authenticated identity, an admin-themed token in the path is the cleanest impersonation tell. Rationale: Anchored on the PoC's literal `CEO-admin-impersonated` segment plus the documented impact: 'Impersonate any user, including administrators.' Privileged-role tokens in the URL segment are the highest-signal impersonation indicator because the vulnerable middleware uses the segment verbatim as `IUser.username`. Corroborated against vulert.com and cvereports.com which both echo the admin-impersonation impact. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://vulert.com/vuln-db/-samanhappy-mcphub--sse-endpoint-accepts-arbitrary-username-from-url-path-without-authentication--en---

Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Tenant where an admin user genuinely has username `admin` / `administrator` (legitimately connecting their own client)
  • Penetration testers running authorized GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf validation
  • Security scanners (Nuclei templates) probing for the CVE
  • Service accounts named with `sysadmin` / `operator` legitimately using MCPHub
  • Synthetic monitoring that intentionally uses an `admin` username to verify the patch
Suppression filter
| where SrcIP !in ("10.0.0.50","10.0.0.51") // sanctioned pentest jump boxes
| where UA !has "Nuclei" and UA !has "DatadogSynthetics"
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm MCPHub package version on Computer. If < 0.12.15 with `enableBearerAuth=false`, treat the alert as a confirmed identity-spoofing attempt. Identify SrcIP and check whether it is internal (employee VPN) or external (internet-facing). 2. Contain: block SrcIP at the perimeter, force-disconnect the SSE session (`pkill node` or restart MCPHub process), upgrade package to >= 0.12.15, enable bearer auth and rotate any bearer keys. 3. Hunt: pivot to the downstream MCP servers (file system, GitHub, database connectors) that were reachable via this MCPHub instance and audit their activity for the spoofed-user time window — the impersonation is upstream but the damage is in the downstream tool calls.
// MCPHub admin-themed identity spoofing (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf)
let AdminTokens = dynamic(["admin","administrator","root","sudo","owner","superuser","sysadmin","ceo","cfo","cto","cio","operator","god","impersonated"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem))
   | extend SrcIP = cIP, Url = csUriStem, UA = csUserAgent, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL))
   | extend SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| mv-apply tok = AdminTokens to typeof(string) on (
    where UserSegment contains tok
    | summarize MatchedTokens = make_set(tok)
  )
| where array_length(MatchedTokens) > 0
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Url, UserSegment, MatchedTokens, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: MCPHub Impersonation Via Admin-Themed Username In SSE URL Path

description: Detects GET requests to the MCPHub `/<user>/sse` endpoint where the user-segment matches privileged-role keywords. Pre-patch (< 0.12.15) MCPHub treats this path segment as the authenticated identity (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf).

MCPHub SSE user-segment fan-out — single source spawning sessions under multiple usernames AIReconnaissance High
Detects a single source IP creating MCPHub SSE sessions under three or more distinct `<user>` URL segments within a 10-minute window — the textbook impersonation-probing / user-enumeration pattern enabled by GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf. Legitimate clients connect under one identity per host. Rationale: Threshold-based: legitimate MCPHub clients connect under one consistent username per host. A SrcIP cycling through 3+ distinct `<user>/sse` segments in 10m is enumeration / impersonation probing — the only realistic explanation given the article's documented `req.params.user` design flaw. Sigma omitted because this is a cross-event aggregation. Datadog query is filter-only; the count/dcount threshold is enforced in the Cloud SIEM rule wrapper (groupBy SrcIP, count_unique UserSegment >= 3). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-WF8Q-WVV8-P8JF
ATT&CKT1087 T1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • NAT'd egress IP behind which multiple legitimate MCPHub users share the same SrcIP (employee VPN concentrator, corporate proxy)
  • Shared CI/CD runner that authenticates several pipeline service identities against MCPHub
  • Multi-tenant MCPHub deployments where one frontend IP fronts many tenants
  • Authorized red-team testing of the CVE
  • Load-test tooling iterating over synthetic user identities
Suppression filter
// Suppress known NAT/proxy egress IPs and CI runners after they've been profiled
| where SrcIP !in ("10.10.10.1","203.0.113.10")   // corp VPN concentrator + CI runner egress
| where DistinctUsers >= 3   // keep the floor; raise if NAT egress baseline higher
Response runbook
1. Triage: list the ObservedUsers set and cross-check against IdentityInfo / HR roster. If any segment is not a real user (e.g. `admin-test`, `impersonated`, random tokens) treat as confirmed. If SrcIP is a known proxy/NAT, normalize by X-Forwarded-For (W3CIISLog: enable XFF logging) and re-evaluate. 2. Contain: block SrcIP at perimeter, terminate active SSE sessions on the MCPHub host, upgrade @samanhappy/mcphub to >= 0.12.15 and switch enableBearerAuth=true. 3. Hunt: for each ObservedUser, query downstream MCP-server tool-call logs for actions credited to that identity within the SSE session window; review database / GitHub / filesystem MCP-server audit trails for unauthorized reads or writes attributed to the impersonated user.
// MCPHub user-segment fan-out — single SrcIP, multiple distinct <user>/sse spoof attempts in 10m
let WindowSize = 10m;
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem)), SrcIP = cIP, Url = csUriStem, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL)), SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| where UserSegment !in~ ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","_next","public")
| summarize
    DistinctUsers = dcount(UserSegment),
    ObservedUsers = make_set(UserSegment, 30),
    Hits = count(),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    SampleUrls = make_set(Url, 10)
    by SrcIP, Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowSize)
| where DistinctUsers >= 3   // empirical fan-out threshold — one legit client = one identity per host
| order by DistinctUsers desc, LastSeen desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:azure.appservices) @http.method:GET (@http.url_details.path:*/sse OR @http.url_details.path:*/sse/*) -@http.url_details.path:/api/* -@http.url_details.path:/static/*
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=GET (Web.url="*/sse" OR Web.url="*/sse/*" OR Web.url="*/sse?*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.dest_port Web.url _time span=10m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rex field=url "^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/(?<user_segment>[^/]+)/sse"
| where isnotnull(user_segment) AND NOT user_segment IN ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","_next","public")
| stats dc(user_segment) as distinct_users values(user_segment) as observed_users values(url) as urls min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime count by src dest _time
| where distinct_users >= 3
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - distinct_users
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=GET (Web.url="*/sse" OR Web.url="*/sse/*" OR Web.url="*/sse?*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.dest_port Web.url _time span=10m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rex field=url "^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/(?<user_segment>[^/]+)/sse"
| where isnotnull(user_segment) AND NOT user_segment IN ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","_next","public")
| stats dc(user_segment) as distinct_users values(user_segment) as observed_users values(url) as urls min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime count by src dest _time
| where distinct_users >= 3
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - distinct_users
MCPHub tool execution via spoofed identity — POST to /<user>/messages with JSON-RPC body AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the second-stage exploitation after a spoofed SSE handshake (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf): POST to `/<user>/messages?sessionId=<uuid>` with a JSON-RPC tool call. This is where the spoofed identity is used to actually invoke MCP tools (filesystem, GitHub, DB connectors) under the impersonated user's authorization context. Rationale: The article's PoC Step 3 explicitly shows `curl -X POST http://TARGET:3100/CEO-admin-impersonated/messages?sessionId=54efc6f5-... -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call",...}'`. The URL shape `/<user>/messages?sessionId=<uuid>` is unique to MCPHub (the JSON-RPC tool-call ingress for the SSE transport) and represents the actual exploitation step — not just probing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf
ATT&CKT1059 T1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MCPHub clients on patched instances invoking tools normally (the URL shape persists post-patch — it's the supported transport)
  • Authorized penetration testing of the CVE
  • Internal AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor) sending tool calls during normal operation
  • Synthetic monitoring exercising tool calls for uptime checks
  • Backup / replication tooling proxying MCP traffic
Suppression filter
// Once instance is patched + bearer auth on, this is benign traffic. Suppress when Authorization header is present.
// W3CIISLog doesn't carry headers; CSL has RequestHeader fields on some proxies — refine when available.
| where SrcIP !in ("10.10.10.20","10.10.10.21")   // sanctioned MCP client subnet
| where UA !has "Claude-Desktop" and UA !has "Cursor" and UA !has "mcp-client"
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract UserSegment + SessionId; correlate with the preceding SSE handshake (UC1/UC2 same SessionId or same SrcIP within seconds). Confirm MCPHub version < 0.12.15 or `enableBearerAuth=false`. Pull request body from reverse-proxy logs if available — JSON-RPC `method` and `params.name` reveal which MCP tool was invoked. 2. Contain: kill the SSE session (restart MCPHub or close the upstream socket), block SrcIP, upgrade to >= 0.12.15, enable bearer auth, rotate any secrets the impersonated tool could have read (DB creds, GitHub tokens, filesystem secrets). 3. Hunt: pivot to each named MCP server's audit log (filesystem.read, github.create_pr, db.query, etc.) for actions attributed to UserSegment in the SessionId's lifetime; assess data exfil and write-side actions; review IdP logs to check whether the spoofed UserSegment is a real privileged user whose downstream credentials may have been used.
// MCPHub tool-call execution against a spoofed SSE session (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf, post-handshake)
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "POST"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/messages$"
   | where csUriQuery has "sessionId="
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"^/([^/]+)/messages", 1, csUriStem),
            SessionId   = extract(@"sessionId=([0-9a-fA-F-]{20,})", 1, csUriQuery),
            SrcIP = cIP, Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UA = csUserAgent, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/messages\?.*sessionId=[0-9a-f-]{20,}"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/messages", 1, RequestURL),
            SessionId   = extract(@"(?i)sessionId=([0-9a-fA-F-]{20,})", 1, RequestURL),
            SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment) and isnotempty(SessionId)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Url, UserSegment, SessionId, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Talos weekly top-prevalent malware hash watch (Coinminer / Injector / W32.Variant) AIInstallation High
Surfaces any execution, image-load, or file-write of the four SHA256/MD5 hashes Cisco Talos published in the 2026-05-14 Threat Source newsletter as the most prevalent malware seen in Talos telemetry that week (Win.Worm.Coinminer VID001.exe, W32.Injector d4aa3e70…_63_Exe.exe, W32.Variant u112417.dat, Auto.90B145 APQ9305.dll). Article-specific because it pins on the exact SHA256/MD5 + Talos detection names from this week's bulletin, not a generic IOC sweep. Rationale: Hash IOCs are deterministic — these four SHA256s and the four MD5s come straight from Cisco Talos's weekly telemetry top-list with named verdicts (Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201, W32.Variant:MalwareXgenMisc.29d4.1201, Auto.90B145.282358.in02). They were corroborated by following each Talos file-reputation URL embedded in the article (talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=<SHA256>) which is Talos's authoritative reputation service confirming the verdict. The example filenames VID001.exe / u112417.dat / APQ9305.dll are renameable and only used as soft secondary signal in Splunk — the SHA256/MD5 are the high-fidelity anchors. FP rate is low because we're hash-pinned; the only realistic FPs are authorized malware sandbox hosts (allowlist them). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-time-of-much-patching-is-coming/ • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59

    | extend SourceTable = "ImProcessCreate"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine ),
  ( ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFileSHA256 in (MaliciousSHA256) or TargetFileMD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
    | extend SourceTable = "ImFileEvent"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileMD5, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

Inbound exploit attempt to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager from known UAT-8616 / Cluster IPs AIExploitation Medium
Detects network connections from the Talos-published exploit-source IPs targeting Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager / vSmart (vManage) management interfaces. Anchors on the specific source IPs Talos attributes to UAT-8616 and Clusters 1-4 exploiting CVE-2026-20182 and the CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122 chain. Rationale: Source IPs are explicitly attributed by Talos to UAT-8616 (CVE-2026-20182) and Clusters 1-4 (CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122). Ports cover vManage HTTPS (443/8443), NETCONF (830), SD-WAN device control (4566), and SSH (22). Cross-checked with Cisco PSIRT advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-auth-bypass and Rapid7's disclosure referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/publicationListing.x • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team / Rapid7 / Talos researcher scans from these IPs (rare)
  • Cisco TAC remote-assist sessions originating from Cisco-owned space (not these IPs but operationally similar)
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonations from a SOAR or VirusTotal/Hybrid-Analysis sensor on the perimeter
  • Legitimate SD-WAN partner / managed-service-provider connections routed through the same upstream ISP CIDR
Suppression filter
| where not(DestinationHostName has_any ("sandbox","honeypot","redteam"))
Response runbook
Triage: confirm the destination is a Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager/Controller and pull vManage audit logs around the connection time looking for new admin sessions, SSH key additions, or NETCONF edit-config calls. Contain: block the source IP at the perimeter, force re-authentication for the affected vManage instance, snapshot the device for forensics, and verify patch status against CVE-2026-20182/20133/20128/20122. Hunt: pivot on the device for JSP file writes (sysv.jsp, conf.jsp, sysinit.jsp, vmurnp_ikp.jsp, 20251117022131.jsp), outbound connections to 194.163.175.135 / 23.27.143.170, and processes containing /tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh.

XenShell / Godzilla / Behinder JSP webshell file write on Cisco SD-WAN Manager AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the specific JSP webshell filenames Talos observed dropped on compromised Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager nodes after exploitation of CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122. Filenames are non-generic and attacker-chosen (20251117022131.jsp, conf.jsp, sysv.jsp, sysinit.jsp, vmurnp_ikp.jsp). Rationale: Filenames 20251117022131.jsp, conf.jsp, sysv.jsp, sysinit.jsp, vmurnp_ikp.jsp are explicitly named by Talos as attacker-dropped XenShell/Godzilla/Behinder variants on the SD-WAN Manager. Generic .jsp creation under vManage webapps directories also catches XenShell variants with rotating names since SD-WAN Manager should not be receiving developer-dropped JSPs in production. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://github.com/BeichenDream/Godzilla
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cisco-supplied upgrade package (.tar.gz) extracting legitimate vendor JSPs during a planned vManage software update
  • Backup/restore operations re-laying webapp content
  • Developer / lab vManage where engineers stage custom JSPs (should not exist in production)
  • WAR file redeployment after a TAC support case
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("tar","gzip","unzip","rpm","dpkg") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vmanage-upgrade","viptela"))
Response runbook
Triage: read the file contents — XenShell and Godzilla shells contain recognisable Base64 payload-decryption logic and parameter-driven cmd execution; capture file hash and compare against published Godzilla/Behinder/XenShell signatures. Contain: quarantine the file, kill the Tomcat/Java process serving the webapp, isolate the SD-WAN Manager from the data-plane, and force admin credential rotation. Hunt: pull access logs for POST requests to the JSP path, pivot on source IPs (look for the cluster IPs listed in UC #1), check for follow-on Bash command execution, SSH key additions in /home/*/.ssh/authorized_keys, and outbound traffic to 194.163.175.135 / 23.27.143.170.
let WebshellNames = dynamic(["20251117022131.jsp","conf.jsp","sysv.jsp","sysinit.jsp","vmurnp_ikp.jsp"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ (WebshellNames)
   or (FileName endswith ".jsp" and FolderPath has_any ("/vmanage/","/webapps/","/opt/web-app/","/tomcat/webapps/"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebshellNames = dynamic(["20251117022131.jsp","conf.jsp","sysv.jsp","sysinit.jsp","vmurnp_ikp.jsp"]);
imFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ (WebshellNames)
   or (TargetFileExtension =~ "jsp" and TargetFilePath has_any ("/vmanage/","/webapps/","/opt/web-app/","/tomcat/webapps/"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AdaptixC2 'shadowcore' / Mythic C2 traffic to UAT-8616 infrastructure 194.163.175.135 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound traffic to the AdaptixC2/Mythic infrastructure Talos attributes to UAT-8616 — IP 194.163.175.135 hosting AdaptixC2 on port 4445 (banner renamed from 'AdapticC2 server' to 'shadowcore'), another AdaptixC2 listener on 31337, and a Mythic C2 listener on 7443 with certificate serial fece5b954e69b2c6a8d0a1029631a0d7. Rationale: 194.163.175.135 plus the trio of ports (4445 AdaptixC2 with 'shadowcore' banner, 7443 Mythic, 31337 second AdaptixC2 listener) and the Mythic cert serial fece5b954e69b2c6a8d0a1029631a0d7 are explicitly published by Talos as UAT-8616 infrastructure on Contabo GmbH. The IP-and-port tuple is high-fidelity because legitimate enterprise traffic to a Contabo VPS on these obscure ports is exceedingly rare. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://github.com/Adaptix-Framework/AdaptixC2 • https://github.com/its-a-feature/Mythic
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573.002 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Certificates.All_Certificates
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team using a leased Contabo VPS at the same IP (verify with Red Team calendar)
  • Threat-intel detonation / sandbox call-out from a security-research host
  • Pen-test engagement where the tester reused public AdaptixC2 infrastructure (rare — most rotate)
  • Researcher running adversary-emulation labs that happen to point at the same C2
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("curl","wget") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("redteam","pentest"))
Response runbook
Triage: identify the initiating process and parent on the source host; correlate against the cert serial fece5b954e69b2c6a8d0a1029631a0d7 in TLS / Zeek x509 logs; confirm whether the source is a Cisco SD-WAN Manager. Contain: block 194.163.175.135 at the perimeter (all ports), isolate the source host, capture memory and a process tree dump. Hunt: pivot to other Contabo /24 neighbours, search for the AdaptixC2 'shadowcore' banner string in Zeek/Suricata SSL logs across 30d, and for Mythic JARM/JA3 fingerprints; check for additional post-compromise actions (SSH key writes, NETCONF edits, /tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh).

DeviceNetworkEvents

| where RemotePort in (C2_Ports) or RemotePort == 22
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc

| where DestinationPort in (C2_Ports)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction, SourceIP, SourcePort, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, ApplicationProtocol, RequestURL
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AdaptixC2 'systemd-resolved' or Sliver 'CWan' implant on Linux / SD-WAN host AIInstallation Medium
Detects the specific implant filenames Talos observed dropped post-exploitation on Cisco SD-WAN devices: 'systemd-resolved' (AdaptixC2 agent masquerading as the legitimate Linux service) calling 194.163.175.135:4445, and 'CWan' (Sliver implant) calling mtls://23.27.143.170:443. Hunts both the file presence and the C2 callouts. Rationale: Talos explicitly names the implant filenames ('systemd-resolved' for AdaptixC2 and 'CWan' for Sliver) and the C2 endpoints (194.163.175.135:4445, mtls://23.27.143.170:443). The masquerade check excludes the legitimate /lib/systemd path for systemd-resolved, so any other path equals a high-fidelity hit. Verified Sliver and AdaptixC2 framework attribution via the public AdaptixC2 and Sliver project pages. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://github.com/BishopFox/sliver • https://github.com/Adaptix-Framework/AdaptixC2
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1059.004 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A patched/upgraded systemd package temporarily executing systemd-resolved from /tmp during install (rare, vendor-signed)
  • Custom systemd build by an internal platform team installing to a non-standard path (verify with platform owner)
  • Sliver red-team engagement using the default 'CWan' name (extremely unlikely — operators rename)
  • Sysadmin script that legitimately greps log lines for 23.27.143.170 / 194.163.175.135 (extremely unlikely without prior alert)
Response runbook
Triage: capture file hash, dump memory of the process, check parent (likely tomcat / jsp shell -> bash). Contain: kill the process, quarantine the binary, isolate the host from the network, and block 194.163.175.135 and 23.27.143.170 at the perimeter. Hunt: review /home/*/.ssh/authorized_keys for new keys, NETCONF edit-config audit logs on vManage/vSmart, /tmp/moneroocean/ presence, and other hosts beaconing to either C2 IP across the last 90 days.

union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where (FileName =~ "systemd-resolved" and FolderPath !in~ (ImpostorPaths))
     or FileName =~ "CWan"
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("194.163.175.135","23.27.143.170")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName),
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where RemoteIP in (C2_IPs)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["194.163.175.135","23.27.143.170"]);
let KeywordList = dynamic(["systemd-resolved","CWan","194.163.175.135","23.27.143.170","mtls://23.27.143.170"]);
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any (KeywordList)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_cwan:
    Image|endswith: '/CWan'
  selection_impostor:
    Image|endswith: '/systemd-resolved'
  filter_legit:
    Image:
      - '/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved'
      - '/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved'
      - '/usr/libexec/systemd/systemd-resolved'
  condition: selection_cwan or (selection_impostor and not filter_legit)
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) ((@process.name:CWan) OR (@process.name:systemd-resolved AND -@process.executable.path:("/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved" OR "/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved" OR "/usr/libexec/systemd/systemd-resolved")) OR @process.command_line:(*194.163.175.135* OR *23.27.143.170*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | (ImageFileName=/\/CWan$/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\/systemd-resolved$/i AND NOT ImageFileName=/^\/(lib|usr\/lib|usr\/libexec)\/systemd\/systemd-resolved$/) OR regex("(194\.163\.175\.135|23\.27\.143\.170)", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="systemd-resolved" AND Processes.process_path!="/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved" AND Processes.process_path!="/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved") OR Processes.process_name="CWan" OR match(Processes.process,"194\.163\.175\.135") OR match(Processes.process,"23\.27\.143\.170") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="systemd-resolved" AND Processes.process_path!="/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved" AND Processes.process_path!="/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved") OR Processes.process_name="CWan" OR match(Processes.process,"194\.163\.175\.135") OR match(Processes.process,"23\.27\.143\.170") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
UAT-8616 post-compromise on SD-WAN: SSH key add, NETCONF edit, su root, XMRig miner.sh AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the specific post-compromise actions Talos lists for UAT-8616 after exploitation of CVE-2026-20182/20127 — adding SSH keys, modifying NETCONF configuration, privilege escalation via 'su root -c id', plus Cluster 7's XMRig deployment via /tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh with config_background.json. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's verbatim strings: Code Block 2 (/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh --config=/tmp/moneroocean/config_background.json), Code Block 3 (su root -c id), and the named post-compromise actions Talos lists for UAT-8616 (SSH key addition, NETCONF configuration modification). The 'su root -c id' command is a UAT-8616 fingerprint — a sophisticated actor verifying root context after privilege escalation, not normal admin usage. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://moneroocean.stream/
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1543 T1548.003 T1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin running 'ssh-copy-id' or a configuration-management tool (Ansible authorized_key module, Salt ssh_auth.present) — these will hit the authorized_keys filter
  • Cisco vManage operators legitimately using NETCONF edit-config for device template pushes
  • An internal Monero mining lab (unlikely in enterprise; if present, exclude by host group)
  • Custom shell scripts that legitimately invoke 'su root -c <cmd>' on appliances during change windows
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("ansible","salt-minion","puppet","chef-client") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ssh-copy-id"))
Response runbook
Triage: identify the parent process — legitimate sysadmin work has an interactive shell ancestor; UAT-8616 activity has tomcat/jsp/sh ancestors from the webshell. Pull the user account, source IP of any preceding SSH/HTTP session, and check vManage audit logs for the corresponding NETCONF transaction ID. Contain: rotate all SSH keys for affected users, revoke unauthorized authorized_keys entries, kill miner processes, remove /tmp/moneroocean/, snapshot the device. Hunt: pivot on the parent chain back to the JSP webshell drop (UC #2), source IPs (UC #1), and outbound to AdaptixC2/Sliver C2 (UC #3, #4); search 90d for the moneroocean.stream domain and pool addresses in DNS logs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "su root" and ProcessCommandLine has "-c" and ProcessCommandLine has "id")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh","config_background.json","moneroocean")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "authorized_keys" and FileName in~ ("bash","sh","tee","echo","cat","dd","cp"))
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "edit-config" and ProcessCommandLine has "netconf")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Keywords = dynamic(["su root -c id","su root \u2013c id","/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh","config_background.json","moneroocean","authorized_keys","edit-config","netconf"]);
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any (Keywords)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, SeverityLevel, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) (@process.command_line:(*"su root"*"-c"*id* OR *"/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh"* OR *config_background.json* OR *moneroocean*) OR (@process.command_line:*authorized_keys* AND @process.name:(bash OR sh OR tee OR echo OR cat OR dd OR cp)) OR (@process.command_line:*edit-config* AND @process.command_line:*netconf*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | (regex("su\\s+root\\s+-c\\s+id", field=CommandLine) OR regex("/tmp/moneroocean/miner\\.sh", field=CommandLine) OR regex("config_background\\.json", field=CommandLine) OR (regex("authorized_keys", field=CommandLine) AND ImageFileName=/\/(bash|sh|tee|echo|cat|dd|cp)$/i) OR (regex("edit-config", field=CommandLine) AND regex("netconf", field=CommandLine))) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*su root*-c*id*","*/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh*","*config_background.json*") OR (Processes.process="*authorized_keys*" AND Processes.process_name IN ("bash","sh","tee","echo","cat")) OR (Processes.process="*edit-config*" AND Processes.process="*netconf*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*su root*-c*id*","*/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh*","*config_background.json*") OR (Processes.process="*authorized_keys*" AND Processes.process_name IN ("bash","sh","tee","echo","cat")) OR (Processes.process="*edit-config*" AND Processes.process="*netconf*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-20182", "CVE-2026-20133", "CVE-2026-20128", "CVE-2026-20122", "CVE-2026-20127")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-20182", "CVE-2026-20133", "CVE-2026-20128", "CVE-2026-20122", "CVE-2026-20127")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

FrostyNeighbor PicassoLoader drop to %AppData%\WinDataScope\Update.js AIInstallation High
Hunts the article-specific second-stage drop: a JavaScript PicassoLoader payload written to a fixed AppData subfolder ('WinDataScope') used by FrostyNeighbor's March 2026 Ukrtelecom-themed compromise chain. The folder name and filename are both fingerprinted by ESET against multiple samples in this campaign. Rationale: WinDataScope is a folder name nowhere referenced in legitimate software inventories — ESET fingerprints it directly to FrostyNeighbor's PicassoLoader staging in the May 2026 report. Combined with the file name Update.js this is a near-zero-FP file-write signature. Cross-checked against: • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240 • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/
ATT&CKT1027.009 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem

  • Threat intel detonation labs writing the IOC to disk

Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName =~ "system")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Hash the file (SHA-1/256) and compare to ESET's published B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC and E15ABEE1CFDE8BE7D87C7C0B510450BAD6BC0906; pull the parent process tree (expect wscript.exe with --update arg). Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host via Defender Live Response or Falcon Network Containment; kill any wscript.exe/cscript.exe running Update.js; remove the WinDataScope folder and any scheduled tasks referencing it. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep org for additional WinDataScope folders, any DNS lookups to needbinding.icu / nebao.icu / algsat.icu / sardk.icu / alexavegas.icu / lavanille.buzz, and ViberPC.dll image loads.

FrostyNeighbor JS dropper self-relaunch with --update flag AIExploitation High
Detects the FrostyNeighbor first-stage JavaScript dropper's documented self-relaunch pattern: wscript.exe / cscript.exe executes a .js file with the literal '--update' argument so the second branch of the script can install PicassoLoader. The flag string is bespoke to this campaign and is not used by legitimate Windows Script Host workflows. Rationale: The article explicitly states the first-stage script re-executes itself with the --update flag to branch into the PicassoLoader drop. The double-dash --update form is uncommon in WSH-launched JavaScript and pairs with a .js argument that is rarely seen in benign workflows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bespoke Windows updater wrappers some sysadmins build using JScript
  • Vendor installers that pass --update to a side-by-side wscript helper
  • RMM tooling using JS-based updater payloads
  • Penetration test simulations referencing the same TTP
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"C:\Program Files\",@"C:\Program Files (x86)\") and InitiatingProcessFileName !endswith "explorer.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Resolve the full .js path from ProcessCommandLine — confirm whether it sits in a user-writable directory (Desktop, Downloads, Temp, %AppData%) which is the FrostyNeighbor pattern. Hash the .js and compare to ESET's published 8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F. Step 2 (contain): Kill the wscript/cscript process tree; quarantine the .js; isolate host. Step 3 (hunt): Look for the parent process — the original execution should be either explorer.exe (manual double-click) or winrar.exe/7z.exe extracting from 53_7.03.2026_R.rar. Also hunt for the WinDataScope drop and outbound DNS to needbinding.icu / nebao.icu.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--update"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--update" and ActingProcessCommandLine has ".js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

FrostyNeighbor C2 callout to needbinding/nebao/algsat/sardk/alexavegas/lavanille AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS or HTTP egress to the six FrostyNeighbor C2 domains published by ESET in May 2026 (PicassoLoader on five .icu hosts plus a .buzz Cobalt Strike host). All six share the same actor infrastructure cluster registered between 2026-03-10 and 2026-04-14. Rationale: ESET published the full domain list in Table 2 of the article alongside first-seen dates from a freshly-registered actor infrastructure cluster (.icu/.buzz, no legitimate corporate use). Any host in a UA/PL/LT/EE government estate touching these domains is high-fidelity actor traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DFIR team detonating samples in a connected analysis VM
  • Threat-intel ingestion proxies fetching the same samples
  • Researcher accessing the article and clicking through to defang links
  • Honeypot connecting to the C2 to fingerprint it
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SenseIR.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Defender\")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the contacting process via InitiatingProcessFileName / ContextImageFileName — for wscript.exe/cscript.exe parents this is almost certainly PicassoLoader. Capture the User-Agent and full URL. Step 2 (contain): Sinkhole the domain at egress (block at firewall + DNS); isolate the host; pull memory and disk image. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the resolved IP — Cloudflare-fronted but the origin may rotate; check for sibling domains on the same naming pattern (*-*.needbinding.icu, attachment-storage-asset-static.needbinding.icu), and hunt for the WinDataScope drop and ViberPC.dll on every host that resolved any of the six domains.
let FrostyDomains = dynamic(["needbinding.icu","nebao.icu","algsat.icu","alexavegas.icu","sardk.icu","lavanille.buzz"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (FrostyDomains)
    | extend Source="NetworkEvent"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source;
let EventHits = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where ActionType =~ "DnsQueryResponse"
    | extend QueriedDomain = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).DnsQueryString)
    | where QueriedDomain has_any (FrostyDomains)
    | extend Source="DnsQuery"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP="", RemoteUrl=QueriedDomain,
              RemotePort=tolong(0),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, Source;
union NetHits, EventHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let FrostyDomains = dynamic(["needbinding.icu","nebao.icu","algsat.icu","alexavegas.icu","sardk.icu","lavanille.buzz"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where DnsQuery has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Domain=DnsQuery, Source="DNS"),
    (ImWebSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where Url has_any (FrostyDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Domain=coalesce(HttpHostName,Url), Source="HTTP"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (FrostyDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr=SourceIP, SrcUsername=SourceUserName, Domain=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Source="FW")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PicassoLoader scheduled-task creation by wscript/cscript after C2 XML fetch AIInstallation Medium
Detects FrostyNeighbor's persistence step: the JavaScript dropper downloads a scheduled-task XML template (served via the misleading Content-Type/Content-Disposition response to a .jpg URL) and then registers it. The parent-child chain of WSH spawning schtasks.exe or powershell.exe Register-ScheduledTask is article-specific. Rationale: The article describes the script downloading 'https://book-happy.needbinding[.]icu/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/1GreenAM.jpg' (which actually returns config.xml with Content-Type: application/xml) and then using it for persistence. Wscript/cscript spawning schtasks /Create /XML is a tight, low-FP pivot specific to this WSH-driven persistence pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Adobe / vendor installer JScript wrappers that schedule a maintenance task
  • Internal MDM scripts that register update tasks via JScript bootstrappers
  • Application Compatibility scripts during corporate imaging
  • RMM agents using a JScript first-stage that registers a service-task
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"C:\Program Files\",@"C:\Program Files (x86)\",@"C:\Windows\CCM\",@"C:\Windows\System32\GroupPolicy\") and AccountName endswith "$")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Dump the scheduled-task XML (schtasks /Query /TN <task> /XML) — the FrostyNeighbor template launches %AppData%\WinDataScope\Update.js on a schedule. Capture parent process tree back to the original .js file under the user profile. Step 2 (contain): schtasks /Delete /TN <task> /F; remove the WinDataScope folder; isolate host; pull memory. Step 3 (hunt): Across the org, look for any scheduled task whose Action.Command points into %AppData%\WinDataScope or whose RegistrationInfo.Source mentions WinDataScope; cross-reference with DNS hits on the six C2 domains.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","/XML"))
      or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ChildProcess=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcess=InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentProcess=InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where (ActingProcessName has "schtasks.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","/XML"))
      or (ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ActingProcessCommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WSH-Initiated Scheduled Task Registration (FrostyNeighbor PicassoLoader)
id: 2c8f47a3-9b14-4ee5-b87e-91a4f5d63c11
description: Detects wscript.exe or cscript.exe spawning schtasks.exe /Create /XML or powershell Register-ScheduledTask. This is the persistence step in FrostyNeighbor's March 2026 PicassoLoader chain, in which an XML template is downloaded under a fake .jpg URL and registered as a scheduled task.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/frostyneighbor-fresh-mischief-digital-shenanigans/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  child_schtasks:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/Create'
      - '/XML'
  child_pwsh:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'Register-ScheduledTask'
  condition: parent and (child_schtasks or child_pwsh)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate vendor installers that use JScript wrappers to register tasks (rare)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\\CSCRIPT.EXE)) ((@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SchTasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*/Create* OR */XML*)) OR (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:*Register-ScheduledTask*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| (ImageFileName=/schtasks\.exe$/i AND regex("(/Create|/XML)", field=CommandLine))
  OR (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND regex("Register-ScheduledTask", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as child_cmdline values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" OR (Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" AND Processes.process="*Register-ScheduledTask*") OR Processes.process_name="taskeng.exe") (Processes.process="*/Create*" OR Processes.process="*Register-ScheduledTask*" OR Processes.process="*/XML*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
FrostyNeighbor Cobalt Strike beacon ViberPC.dll image load AIInstallation Medium
Detects loading of ViberPC.dll, the final-stage Cobalt Strike beacon FrostyNeighbor masquerades as the legitimate Viber desktop messenger DLL. ESET publishes a SHA-1 (43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB) and the file is expected outside the legitimate Viber install path under the standard Cobalt Strike beacon naming pattern Win32/CobaltStrike.Beacon.S. Rationale: ESET published the exact SHA-1 (43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB) for the ViberPC.dll Cobalt Strike beacon in Table 1, classified Win32/CobaltStrike.Beacon.S. Combined with masquerading detection — ViberPC.dll loaded from a non-Viber path — this is a high-confidence final-stage beacon detection. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1055.001 T1588.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Viber portable install on a corporate device outside standard install paths
  • DFIR / red-team Cobalt Strike training exercise with renamed loader
  • Backup software restoring a snapshot containing the IOC
  • File-server hosting a software repository with the sample present
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any (@"\Program Files\Viber\",@"\Program Files (x86)\Viber\",@"\AppData\Local\Viber\") and SHA1 !in~ ("43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Hash-verify the loaded DLL against ESET's published SHA-1; capture the loading process (often rundll32.exe, regsvr32.exe, or a sacrificial process injected by PicassoLoader). Pull memory of the loading process for beacon config extraction. Step 2 (contain): Isolate host via EDR; block hash org-wide; sinkhole nama-belakang.nebao.icu and best-seller.lavanille.buzz at egress. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep all hosts for ViberPC.dll outside the Viber install path; pivot on beacon C2 IP after extracting the malleable profile; check AAD/SigninLogs for anomalous interactive logons from any host that loaded the beacon (lateral-movement indicator).
let FrostyHashes = dynamic(["43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"]);
let ImageLoads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FileName =~ "ViberPC.dll"
    | where SHA1 in~ (FrostyHashes)
         or not (FolderPath has @"\Viber\" or FolderPath has @"\Program Files\Viber")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="ImageLoad";
let FileWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FileName =~ "ViberPC.dll"
    | where SHA1 in~ (FrostyHashes)
         or not (FolderPath has @"\Viber\" or FolderPath has @"\Program Files\Viber")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="FileWrite";
union ImageLoads, FileWrites
| order by Timestamp desc
