Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:

let LookbackDays = 7d;

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or SHA1 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or MD5 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or SHA1 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or MD5 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud npm Worm C2 callback to Session Protocol CDN and masscan.cloud AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or outbound TCP/UDP to the Session Protocol seed nodes (seed1.getsession.org, filev2.getsession.org) and api.masscan.cloud used by TeamPCP's Mini Shai-Hulud worm to exfiltrate harvested CI/CD secrets and developer credentials. These hostnames are not part of any legitimate enterprise software supply chain and any contact is high-fidelity. Rationale: Domains seed1.getsession.org, filev2.getsession.org, and api.masscan.cloud are named explicitly as the worm's exfiltration channel in the StepSecurity write-up. Session Protocol nodes have zero legitimate enterprise use and api.masscan.cloud is the same C2 infrastructure observed across the @antv variant (memory observation 1252) — high-fidelity primary IOCs across multiple StepSecurity / Socket.dev / JFrog reports on the campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer running the Session Messenger desktop app on a corp workstation (rare; whitelist by user)
  • Security researchers detonating the worm in an authorized sandbox host
  • Internal red team replaying campaign IOCs during a purple-team exercise
  • Threat-intel platforms (MISP, OpenCTI) performing connectivity checks against indicator URLs
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("session.exe","Session.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("session.exe","Session.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Identify the InitiatingProcessFileName / ContextImageFileName — confirm it is node, npm, bun, git, or a CI runner process (and not Session Messenger). Pivot on DeviceId to list every package install in the prior 24h on that host. Step 2 (Contain): Isolate the device via Defender Live Response, force-rotate all credentials in scope (npm tokens, GitHub PATs, cloud keys, .env values), and revoke OIDC trust on the affected GitHub Actions repo. Step 3 (Hunt): Across the org, sweep DeviceFileEvents for router_init.js drops and DeviceProcessEvents for any commit authored as claude@users.noreply.github.com in the last 14d to find every laterally-infected publisher.
let CampaignHosts = dynamic(["seed1.getsession.org","filev2.getsession.org","api.masscan.cloud"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignHosts) or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) in~ (CampaignHosts)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Indicator=coalesce(RemoteUrl, RemoteIP), Source="network", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName;
let EvHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionFailed","NetworkConnectionEvents")
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignHosts) or AdditionalFields has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Indicator=coalesce(RemoteUrl, tostring(AdditionalFields)), Source="device-event", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName=tostring(parse_json(""));
NetHits
| union EvHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignHosts = dynamic(["seed1.getsession.org","filev2.getsession.org","api.masscan.cloud"]);
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator=Name, Source="DnsEvents";
let AsimDns = ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, Source="ImDnsActivity";
let ProxyHits = CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (CampaignHosts) or RequestURL has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Source="Proxy/CEF";
let WebHits = ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (CampaignHosts) or Url has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), Source="ImWebSession";
DnsHits | union AsimDns, ProxyHits, WebHits
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count() by Computer, ClientIP, Indicator, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

  - Legitimate use of Session Messenger desktop client by a developer (rare in enterprise)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) ((@EventID:22 AND (@QueryName:seed1.getsession.org OR @QueryName:filev2.getsession.org OR @QueryName:api.masscan.cloud)) OR (@EventID:3 AND (@DestinationHostname:seed1.getsession.org OR @DestinationHostname:filev2.getsession.org OR @DestinationHostname:api.masscan.cloud)) OR @network.destination.domain:(seed1.getsession.org OR filev2.getsession.org OR api.masscan.cloud))

TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud stealer payload hash match (SHA256/SHA1) AIInstallation High
Alerts on disk-write or in-memory execution of a binary whose SHA256 or SHA1 matches the obfuscated 2.3 MB credential-stealer payload published by TeamPCP across @tanstack, @uipath, @draftlab and other compromised npm packages. The hashes are the cleanest single-source-of-truth IOCs in this campaign and are reused unchanged across all 50+ compromised package versions. Rationale: Four SHA256 and three SHA1 hashes were published in the StepSecurity article as the canonical fingerprint of the 2.3 MB obfuscated stealer payload. These hashes were observed unchanged across all listed @tanstack/@uipath/@draftlab versions and were corroborated in earlier @antv variant reporting (Socket.dev, JFrog, StepSecurity — memory observations 1249, 1250, 1252). Hash-based hunting carries zero ambiguity and zero FP risk against benign software. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized sandbox detonation by malware researchers on a forensic workstation
  • Internal threat-hunting team running yara/hash sweeps that touch the artifact during analysis
  • Backup or DLP product scanning a quarantined file and re-hashing it
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has "\\SandboxAnalysis\\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("yara.exe","yara64.exe","capa.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Pivot on DeviceId to the InitiatingProcessCommandLine — confirm the parent is npm/node/bun/yarn, then enumerate which package and version installed (look in npm-cache or package-lock.json on the host). Step 2 (Contain): Isolate host, kill node/bun processes, force-rotate every credential reachable from that machine (npm tokens, GH PATs, cloud keys, AI tool keys, wallets, messaging app tokens), revoke any OIDC trust the host's CI runner role had. Step 3 (Hunt): Sweep org for the file hash on every host AND query DeviceFileEvents for any router_init.js drop in node_modules in the last 30d to find lateral worm spread.
let StealerSha256 = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c","0c0e873033875f1bc471eda37e3b9d0f9b89bd41a4bbb4f86746caa2176c40aa","2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96","7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b"]);
let StealerSha1 = dynamic(["79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c","de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd","bbbca2ddaa5d8feaa63e36b76fdaad77386f024f"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where SHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or SHA1 in~ (StealerSha1) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in~ (StealerSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="DeviceProcessEvents";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where SHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or SHA1 in~ (StealerSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="DeviceFileEvents";
let ImgHits = DeviceImageLoadEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where SHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or SHA1 in~ (StealerSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents";
ProcHits | union FileHits, ImgHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let StealerSha256 = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c","0c0e873033875f1bc471eda37e3b9d0f9b89bd41a4bbb4f86746caa2176c40aa","2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96","7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b"]);

  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where FileHashValue in~ (StealerSha256) or FileHashValue in~ (StealerSha1)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer="", User="", FileName, FilePath="", Hash=FileHashValue, ProcessName="", Source="ThreatIntelligenceIndicator";
FileHits | union ProcHits, TiHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud router_init.js dropped at npm package root in node_modules AIInstallation High
Detects file writes of a router_init.js file directly at a package root inside node_modules with a size > 1 MB on a single line — the exact filesystem signature documented in the StepSecurity comparison of clean (1.166.42) vs compromised (1.166.48) @tanstack tarballs (2,341,681 bytes, single line). Catches the worm at install time before the preinstall payload executes. Rationale: Table 2 in the article (Clean 1.166.42 vs Compromised 1.166.48) explicitly identifies router_init.js at root, 2,341,681 bytes, single line, as the structural marker of every compromised tarball. The file is absent from clean versions and is the worm's first-stage loader — file create from npm/node into node_modules is the exact moment of compromise. Cross-checked against the @antv variant analysis (memory observation 1247) which also noted the same loader file pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1027 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate package coincidentally shipping a router_init.js at root (validate by hash — non-stealer hash + size != 2.3 MB single-line is FP)
  • Internal monorepo with a custom build step that generates router_init.js under node_modules cache
  • Developer extracting/inspecting the malicious tarball in a sandbox without executing
Suppression filter
| where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c","0c0e873033875f1bc471eda37e3b9d0f9b89bd41a4bbb4f86746caa2176c40aa","2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96","7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or FileSize between (2000000 .. 3500000)
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Capture SHA256 of the file and compare against the four known stealer hashes; check the package.json and package-lock.json in the parent directory to identify which compromised package landed on disk. Step 2 (Contain): Quarantine host, kill node processes, remove the node_modules tree, force-rotate any tokens stored in npm/git config on the host (npm tokens, GitHub PATs, ~/.aws/credentials, wallet seeds). Step 3 (Hunt): Search org for all npm publish events in last 30d from this user/runner identity AND for any GitHub commit authored as claude@users.noreply.github.com to find onward worm spread.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "router_init.js"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where FileSize > 1000000  // clean tarball baseline is no router_init.js; compromised version is ~2.3MB single line
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm","node","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe","bun","corepack.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileCreate","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "router_init.js"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where TargetFileSize > 1000000
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","corepack")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud router_init.js Drop in npm node_modules
id: a1c9d3e2-8a5d-4f1c-9d2e-1a8b3c5d7e09
description: Detects creation of router_init.js inside a node_modules tree by an npm/node/pnpm/yarn/bun process — TeamPCP's worm signature.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_file:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\router_init.js'
    TargetFilename|contains: '\node_modules\'
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '\corepack.exe'
  condition: selection_file and selection_proc
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate npm package that ships a top-level router_init.js (verify by hash against the four known stealer SHA256s before suppressing)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\node_modules\\*\\router_init.js OR *\\node_modules\\*\\Router_Init.js OR *\\node_modules\\*\\ROUTER_INIT.JS OR */node_modules/*/router_init.js) @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR */bin/node OR */bin/npm)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/[\\\/]node_modules[\\\/].*[\\\/]router_init\.js$/i
| WrittenBytes>1000000
| ContextImageFileName=/(node|npm|pnpm|yarn|bun|corepack)\.exe$/i OR ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|npm|pnpm|yarn|bun|corepack)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, WrittenBytes], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="router_init.js" Filesystem.file_path="*node_modules*" (Filesystem.file_size>1000000 OR Filesystem.file_size="*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="router_init.js" Filesystem.file_path="*node_modules*" (Filesystem.file_size>1000000 OR Filesystem.file_size="*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Mini Shai-Hulud dead-drop git commit authored as claude@users.noreply.github.com AIActions on Objectives High
Detects git commit / push activity where the author email is claude@users.noreply.github.com — TeamPCP's exfiltration signature where stolen secrets are written to attacker-controlled branches via GitHub's GraphQL API, disguised with Dependabot-style branch names drawn from Frank Herbert's Dune universe. Watch for both git.exe invocations and proxied GraphQL commit metadata. Rationale: The article calls out claude@users.noreply.github.com as the verbatim author identity used for every dead-drop commit, paired with Dependabot-style Dune-themed branch names. This email is not a legitimate GitHub-issued no-reply for any real Anthropic/Claude integration and any commit signed with it is attacker activity. The literal string is high-fidelity and zero-collision across enterprise git telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001 T1078.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually testing a phishing-style impersonation in a controlled sandbox repo
  • Internal red-team replaying the worm's commit author for a tabletop exercise
  • Git hook validation tooling parsing the article body text into a log line
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "--dry-run" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("sandboxhost.exe","detonator.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Pivot DeviceId → identify whether the commit was driven by an interactive user shell or a CI runner; pull the remote URL from the git invocation and check for Dependabot-styled branch names containing Dune lore (arrakis, fremen, harkonnen, shai-hulud, muad'dib). Step 2 (Contain): Force-delete the dead-drop branch on GitHub, revoke the runner's OIDC trust + any PAT/installation token that authored it, isolate the host. Step 3 (Hunt): GitHub audit-log sweep for every repo under the same org that received a push from the runner identity in the last 14d; correlate with router_init.js drops (UC 'Mini Shai-Hulud router_init.js dropped in npm package').
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","git") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "commit" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--author","user.email"))
| extend DuneBranchHint = extract(@"(?i)dependabot[-_/]+(arrakis|fremen|paul|atreides|harkonnen|leto|muad'dib|muaddib|shai-hulud|stilgar|gurney|duncan|chani|jessica|spice|melange|sardaukar|bene-gesserit|kwisatz)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, DuneBranchHint
| order by Timestamp desc
let ProcHits = SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/git"
  | where CommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, ProcessName=NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="SecurityEvent4688";
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any ("git.exe","/git")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="ImProcessCreate";
ProcHits | union AsimHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud Dead-Drop Git Commit (claude@users.noreply.github.com)
id: 5e7a1c0a-9b3f-4d2e-8f56-2c4a1f6b8d3e
description: Detects git.exe invocations whose command line embeds claude@users.noreply.github.com — TeamPCP's worm exfiltration author identity.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\git.exe'
  selection_email:
    CommandLine|contains: 'claude@users.noreply.github.com'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_email
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate user of the GitHub Claude app committing on behalf of an authorised AI assistant (validate by repo policy)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security OR linux.auditd) (@EventID:(1 OR 4688) OR @auditd.type:EXECVE) (@Image:(*\\git.exe OR *\\Git.exe OR *\\GIT.EXE) OR @process.name:git OR @process.executable.path:*/git) @CommandLine:*claude@users.noreply.github.com*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/[\\\/]git(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("claude@users\.noreply\.github\.com", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="git.exe" OR Processes.process_name="git") (Processes.process="*claude@users.noreply.github.com*" OR Processes.process="*-c user.email=claude@users.noreply.github.com*" OR Processes.process="*GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=claude@users.noreply.github.com*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="git.exe" OR Processes.process_name="git") (Processes.process="*claude@users.noreply.github.com*" OR Processes.process="*-c user.email=claude@users.noreply.github.com*" OR Processes.process="*GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=claude@users.noreply.github.com*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Node/npm/Bun process enumerating cloud, wallet, AI, and messaging credential file paths AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for node, npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun processes touching the high-value credential file paths that Mini Shai-Hulud's 2.3 MB stealer iterates over (the article cites 100+ paths spanning cloud providers, crypto wallets, AI tools, and messaging apps). The stealer rapidly opens many of these in a single process lifetime — a single-file hit is weak, the fan-out is the signal. Rationale: The article specifies that the 2.3 MB obfuscated payload harvests credentials from 'over 100 file paths spanning cloud providers, cryptocurrency wallets, AI tools, and messaging apps' — and installs persistence in Claude Code and VS Code. A single file touch by node is noise; a fan-out to 6+ distinct cred paths by one node process in seconds is the worm's signature. Sigma omitted because this detection inherently requires a dcount/threshold aggregation. False-positive scenarios filtered by excluding IDE auto-launches. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1005 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • dotenv-cli or similar tool legitimately reading multiple .env files during a build
  • VS Code / Cursor / Claude Code legitimately enumerating user settings + extension state on startup
  • A CLI tool like aws-sdk-js or @aws-amplify/cli walking ~/.aws and ~/.config in one go
  • CI/CD setup scripts (e.g. setup-gcloud, setup-kubectl) caching cred files on a runner before the build
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe","webstorm64.exe","idea64.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "setup-gcloud" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "@aws-amplify/cli" and not (DistinctPaths < 10 and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("webpack","vite","tsc"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Pull InitiatingProcessCommandLine to identify what package the node process was running (look for an installed compromised package from the StepSecurity list); confirm DistinctPaths > 6 within < 60 seconds (stealer is fast; dev tools are spread out). Step 2 (Contain): Kill the node process tree, isolate the host, force-rotate every credential the access list touched (cloud keys, gh tokens, wallet seeds, Slack/Discord/Telegram session tokens), revoke OIDC trust on any GH Actions runner that ran this. Step 3 (Hunt): Correlate the device with router_init.js drops and outbound traffic to seed1.getsession.org / api.masscan.cloud; sweep the org for every host where the same compromised package version was installed via npm-cache enumeration.
let CredPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"\.aws\config", @".npmrc", @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml",
  @"\.config\gcloud\", @"\.azure\accessTokens.json", @"\.kube\config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"\.ssh\id_", @"\AppData\Roaming\Claude",
  @"\AppData\Roaming\Cursor", @"\AppData\Roaming\Code\User\globalStorage",
  "wallet.dat", @"\Local Extension Settings\", @"\Slack\Cookies",
  @"\Discord\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata",
  ".env", @"\Local\Programs\Ollama", @"\.netrc"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or FileName has_any (CredPaths)
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe")  // strip dev IDEs auto-reading own settings
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), DistinctPaths=dcount(FolderPath), SamplePaths=make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"\\",FileName), 10)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where DistinctPaths >= 6   // empirical: stealer fan-out >> any single legit operation
| order by LastSeen desc
let CredPathsAny = dynamic([
  "\\.aws\\credentials","\\.aws\\config",".npmrc","\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml",
  "\\.config\\gcloud\\","\\.azure\\accessTokens.json","\\.kube\\config",
  "\\.docker\\config.json","\\.ssh\\id_","\\AppData\\Roaming\\Claude",
  "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Cursor","\\AppData\\Roaming\\Code\\User\\globalStorage",
  "wallet.dat","\\Local Extension Settings\\","\\Slack\\Cookies",
  "\\Discord\\Local Storage\\leveldb","\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata",".env","\\.netrc"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","corepack")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPathsAny) or TargetFileName has_any (CredPathsAny)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), DistinctPaths=dcount(TargetFilePath), SamplePaths=make_set(TargetFilePath, 10)
          by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| where DistinctPaths >= 6
| order by LastSeen desc

(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| ContextImageFileName=/(node|npm|pnpm|yarn|bun|corepack)(\.exe)?$/i

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function={count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctPaths) | min(_time, as=FirstSeen) | max(_time, as=LastSeen)})

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.

    activity.

            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45321")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45321")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"

          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:

let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79"]);

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload dropped under node_modules (router_init.js / tanstack_runner.js / known SHA256)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Mini Shai-Hulud Is Back: npm Worm Hits over 160 Packages, including Mistral and
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Bun spawned with tanstack_runner.js via npm prepare lifecycle (Mini Shai-Hulud) · [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud persistence to ~/.claude/hooks and .vscode/tasks.json by node/npm/bun · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload dropped under node_modules (router_init.js / tanstack_runner.js / known SHA256) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the file-drop stage of the TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm (May 2026 wave) where compromised @tanstack / @squawk / @uipath / @tallyui / @mistralai / @beproduct / @draftauth / @draftlab tarballs unpack three named JavaScript payloads (router_init.js, router_runtime.js, tanstack_runner.js) into node_modules — or any file matching the two confirmed SHA256s. Triggers on developer workstations and CI runners during `npm install` / `pnpm install` / `yarn install` / `bun install`. Rationale: router_init.js, router_runtime.js and tanstack_runner.js are campaign-unique filenames called out in the Aikido article and corroborated by Socket, StepSecurity, Snyk and Wiz; the two SHA256s are directly from the article's IOC table. File-drop into node_modules combined with a node/npm/bun/pnpm/yarn initiator narrows scope to dependency-install activity, virtually eliminating FPs. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://snyk.io/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-tanstack-more-npm-packages-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises.html

   or SHA256 in ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c","2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96")
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","bun.exe","bun","yarn.cmd","yarn")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

   or TargetFileSHA256 in ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c","2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96")

Bun spawned with tanstack_runner.js via npm prepare lifecycle (Mini Shai-Hulud) AIInstallation High
Catches the execution stage of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm: `bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1` invoked from the @tanstack/setup optional-dependency prepare hook during `npm install`. The parent is node/npm/pnpm/yarn and the commandline references either tanstack_runner.js, @tanstack/setup, or the campaign's git commit hash 79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c. Rationale: The article explicitly documents `bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1` as the prepare-hook execution and pins the trigger to the @tanstack/setup Git dependency at commit 79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c — all three strings are uniquely tied to this campaign. Bun is rarely a child of node/npm in normal CI outside of TanStack ecosystems, and any match including the commit hash is essentially zero-FP. Cross-checked against Socket and StepSecurity write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/tanstack-router-packages-hit-by-coordinated-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546 T1059.007

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("bun.exe","bun")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("tanstack_runner.js","@tanstack/setup")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","yarn.cmd","yarn","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("\\bun.exe","/bun") or TargetProcessName =~ "bun"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("tanstack_runner.js","@tanstack/setup")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","cmd.exe","powershell","bash","/sh")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud persistence to ~/.claude/hooks and .vscode/tasks.json by node/npm/bun AIInstallation High
Catches the worm's developer-workstation persistence stage: after credential theft, the Mini Shai-Hulud payload writes copies of itself into Claude Code's hook directory (`~/.claude/hooks/`) and the VS Code task runner (`.vscode/tasks.json`) so it re-executes across reboots and editor relaunches. Initiator is a JavaScript runtime (node/npm/bun/pnpm/yarn), which is highly unusual for these specific paths. Rationale: The .claude/hooks and .vscode/tasks.json persistence is not in the Aikido article body but is confirmed by Socket and StepSecurity write-ups of the same May 2026 wave — both name these exact paths as the worm's mechanism to survive across reboots and extend infection from CI into developer workstations. A JavaScript runtime writing into either path is anomalous (these are normally edited by humans / the IDE itself), making this a high-fidelity pivot. Drop this UC if Claude Code is not in use anywhere in the estate. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised-mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem
ATT&CKT1546 T1547 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.claude\hooks" or FolderPath has "/.claude/hooks")
   or (FileName =~ "tasks.json" and (FolderPath has @"\.vscode" or FolderPath has "/.vscode"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm","bun.exe","bun","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","yarn.cmd","yarn")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\hooks" or TargetFilePath has "/.claude/hooks")
   or (TargetFileName =~ "tasks.json" and (TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode" or TargetFilePath has "/.vscode"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","bun","pnpm","yarn")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45321")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45321")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"

TanStack Npm Packages Compromised Inside The Mini Shai Hulud Supply Chain Attack

Snyk
2026-05-11 12 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On May 11, 2026, the Mini Shai-Hulud worm compromised 84 npm package artifacts across 42 @tanstack/* packages (as well as @squawk/*, @mistralai/* packages, and others) by chaining a GitHub Actions "Pwn Request," cache poisoning, and OIDC token extraction from runner memory — producing the first npm supply chain attack with valid SLSA Build Level 3 attestations. Here's what happened, what was stolen, and what you need to do right now.

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — TanStack Npm Packages Compromised Inside The Mini Shai Hulud Supply Chain Attack
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 (TanStack/TeamPCP) worm payload file created in node_modules
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Session/Oxen P2P exfil DNS or TCP to getsession.org from build/CI host · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 (TanStack/TeamPCP) worm payload file created in node_modules AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the smuggled payload artifacts (router_init.js, tanstack_runner.js, vite_setup.mjs) that the May 11 2026 TanStack supply chain attack injected into compromised npm tarballs. These filenames are not declared in any legitimate package.json `files` field, so any FileCreated event for them inside a node_modules path is high-fidelity evidence of an affected install. Rationale: router_init.js / tanstack_runner.js / vite_setup.mjs are explicitly named in the Snyk article as smuggled tarball artifacts and the prepare-hook target (`bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1`). They are not in any legitimate TanStack source tree, so a file-creation event under node_modules is a true-positive indicator. Hashes ab4fc...266c and 2ec78d...fc96 are the file SHA256s extracted for this campaign; the master-key hash 0c0e87...da was deliberately excluded (it is a PBKDF2 key, not a file hash). Cross-referenced against prior-session corroboration of the TeamPCP campaign family (mem-obs 305, 317-322) and OSSF MAL-2026-3432 / GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://security.snyk.io/ • https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages (MAL-2026-3432)
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027

title: Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 (TanStack/TeamPCP) Worm Payload File Created in node_modules
id: a3c8d4f1-2b3c-4d5e-9f6a-7b8c9d0e1f2a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects creation of payload files (router_init.js, tanstack_runner.js, vite_setup.mjs)
  inside any node_modules path. These filenames are smuggled into compromised npm
  package tarballs from the May 11 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud (Wave 4) campaign attributed
  to TeamPCP. router_init.js is a 2.3 MB obfuscated payload that is not declared in
  any legitimate package.json `files` field; tanstack_runner.js is invoked from the
  injected optionalDependency `prepare` lifecycle hook (`bun run tanstack_runner.js && exit 1`).
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/tanstack-npm-packages-compromised/
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/13
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1027
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\router_init.js'
      - '/router_init.js'
      - '\tanstack_runner.js'
      - '/tanstack_runner.js'
      - '\vite_setup.mjs'
      - '/vite_setup.mjs'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains: 'node_modules'
  condition: selection_name and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - None expected — these filenames do not appear in any clean TanStack/Mistral/UiPath tarball.
level: high

Session/Oxen P2P exfil DNS or TCP to getsession.org from build/CI host AICommand & Control High
Hunts the Wave 4 worm's exfiltration channel: encrypted upload to filev2.getsession.org plus seed{1,2,3}.getsession.org Session network nodes. This P2P messenger infrastructure has no legitimate use in CI runners or developer build hosts, and the campaign uses it precisely because IP-blocking is ineffective — DNS is the practical perimeter control. Rationale: filev2.getsession.org and seed{1,2,3}.getsession.org are explicitly named in the Snyk article as the Wave 4 exfil endpoints, with the author noting *.getsession.org DNS-level blocking is the practical perimeter control. Session is a niche P2P messenger; legitimate enterprise CI/build traffic to these domains is effectively zero, giving very high fidelity. Cross-checked against prior-session corroboration of the TeamPCP campaign (mem-obs 305, 317-322) which confirms shared exfil patterns across the Bitwarden CLI / SAP / TanStack waves. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://security.snyk.io/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog (TeamPCP attribution)
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1041 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let _sessionDomains = dynamic(["getsession.org","filev2.getsession.org","seed1.getsession.org","seed2.getsession.org","seed3.getsession.org"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  ( DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl endswith "getsession.org"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="NetworkEvent", Indicator=RemoteUrl,
              RemoteIP, RemotePort,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName ),

              RemoteIP=tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).IPAddresses),
              RemotePort=int(null),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName )
| extend LikelyBuildHost = InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","npm.exe","npm","pnpm.exe","pnpm","yarn.exe","yarn","Runner.Worker.exe","Runner.Worker")
| order by Timestamp desc

  ( DnsEvents

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort

| order by conn_count desc

            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
