Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1027

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'

            - 'Invoke-Expression'

            - 'Net.WebClient'

level: high

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:

      article before alerting.
level: medium

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14") or SHA1 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14") or MD5 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14") or SHA1 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14") or MD5 in~ ("799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["799BB5127CA54239D3D4A14367DB3B712012CF14"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ScarCruft sqgame supply-chain delivery domain contact (BirdCall/RokRAT)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — A rigged game: ScarCruft compromises gaming platform in a supply-chain attack
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BirdCall trojanized APK/mono.dll SHA1 match on Windows endpoints · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] BirdCall RokRAT cloud-storage C2 beacon (Dropbox/pCloud) from non-browser process · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
ScarCruft sqgame supply-chain delivery domain contact (BirdCall/RokRAT) AIDelivery High
Hunts for Windows endpoint or DNS contact with the trojanized Yanbian gaming platform domains (sqgame.net, sqgame.com.cn, xiazai.sqgame.com.cn) which delivered the BirdCall/RokRAT backdoor via a malicious mono.dll update package. Any contact from a managed host warrants investigation as the article confirms the update channel was malicious from late 2024. Rationale: sqgame.net, sqgame.com.cn and xiazai.sqgame.com.cn are explicitly identified by ESET as the supply-chain delivery domains. Any contact is high-fidelity since these are not general-purpose services outside Yanbian-region gamers. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0067/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Yanbian-region users with the genuine clean Windows installer downloading non-malicious updates
  • Threat intel researchers detonating samples in sandboxes connected to corporate telemetry
  • Security tools (URLScan, VirusTotal Hunting) crawling the domains
  • DNS over HTTPS resolvers being queried for the domain as part of passive enumeration
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sqgame","mono.dll","20240429.zip")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the host, user, and initiating process. Confirm whether the host has the sqgame Windows client installed (look for mono.dll under the install path) and check timestamps against the malicious update window (late 2024–Dec 2025). Step 2 (contain): Isolate the device via Defender Live Response; block sqgame.net, sqgame.com.cn, xiazai.sqgame.com.cn at the proxy/DNS firewall; quarantine the local sqgame client and mono.dll. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the host for BirdCall/RokRAT IOCs — RokRAT staged Ruby/Python loaders, persistence under HKCU\\Run, and outbound Dropbox/pCloud API traffic; sweep telemetry for any other host that resolved sqgame domains in the past 18 months.
let SqgameDomains = dynamic(["sqgame.net","sqgame.com.cn","xiazai.sqgame.com.cn"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (SqgameDomains)
   or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) has_any (SqgameDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SqgameDomains = dynamic(["sqgame.net","sqgame.com.cn","xiazai.sqgame.com.cn"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where Name has_any (SqgameDomains)
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Domain=Name, QueryType, Source="DnsEvents"),
    (ImDnsActivity
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where DnsQuery has_any (SqgameDomains)
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Domain=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Source="ImDnsActivity"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
     | where RequestURL has_any (SqgameDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (SqgameDomains)
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Domain=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), QueryType="HTTP", Source="CommonSecurityLog"))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BirdCall trojanized APK/mono.dll SHA1 match on Windows endpoints AIInstallation Medium
Alerts on the exact ESET-confirmed SHA1 hashes of the BirdCall-trojanized Yanbian gaming APKs (ybht.apk, sqybhs.apk) appearing on Windows endpoints, or on file events touching the malicious mono.dll update artefact (xiazai.sqgame.com.cn/dating/20240429.zip). Catches enterprise-managed analyst workstations or BYO-laptop sync that pulled the malicious payload. Rationale: Both SHA1 hashes (03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF and FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9) and the filenames ybht.apk, sqybhs.apk, 20240429.zip are explicitly listed in ESET's IOC table and code blocks. Hash-based file detection has near-zero FP outside of analyst sample handling. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0067/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analysts intentionally storing or transferring the samples on managed workstations
  • Threat-intel feed ingestion pipelines writing IOC payloads to disk during enrichment
  • EDR scanning a quarantine folder containing previously caught samples
  • Legitimate Yanbian-region users with sqgame installed (rare in corporate fleet)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has "\\AnalystSandbox\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has "\\Quarantine\\"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the file landed via end-user download (FileOriginUrl/FileOriginReferrerUrl) versus analyst sandbox path. Note process ancestry (browser → APK download is high concern). Step 2 (contain): Isolate device, quarantine matched files, force AV full scan, revoke active user sessions and reset password as Android-side device may be paired. Step 3 (hunt): For Android case, request MDM/Intune logs for the user's mobile device — pivot on package names com.sqgame.* and BirdCall persistence; for Windows case, look for RokRAT staging (Ruby/Python script execution from user temp directories), HKCU\\Run persistence entries written shortly after the file landed, and Dropbox/pCloud API outbound connections from non-browser processes.
let BadSha1 = dynamic(["03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF","FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9"]);
let BadNames = dynamic(["ybht.apk","sqybhs.apk","20240429.zip"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in~ (BadSha1)
   or FileName in~ (BadNames)
   or (FileName =~ "mono.dll" and FolderPath has "sqgame")
   or FileOriginUrl has_any ("sqgame.net","sqgame.com.cn","xiazai.sqgame.com.cn")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadSha1 = dynamic(["03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF","FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9"]);
let BadNames = dynamic(["ybht.apk","sqybhs.apk","20240429.zip"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadSha1)
   or TargetFileName in~ (BadNames)
   or (TargetFileName =~ "mono.dll" and TargetFilePath has "sqgame")
| project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BirdCall RokRAT cloud-storage C2 beacon (Dropbox/pCloud) from non-browser process AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for the BirdCall/RokRAT command-and-control pattern: backdoor processes making API calls to Dropbox or pCloud cloud storage outside of normal browser/sync-client context. ESET explicitly states BirdCall uses Dropbox/pCloud as its primary C2 channel, so non-browser beaconing to api.dropboxapi.com / content.dropboxapi.com / api.pcloud.com from unusual process trees is high-signal. Rationale: ESET explicitly states BirdCall uses Dropbox and pCloud as C2 channels. Pairing the cloud-API destination with a non-browser/non-sync-client process tree is the high-fidelity pivot — bare cloud-API traffic alone is noise. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/rigged-game-scarcruft-compromises-gaming-platform-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PowerShell/Python scripts run by developers using Dropbox/pCloud SDKs for legitimate automation
  • Backup utilities written in C++/Go that use the Dropbox API without registering as the official client
  • CI agents or RPA bots syncing artefacts to cloud storage
  • Curl/wget invocations to api.dropboxapi.com for legitimate file pulls (CDN-style)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !endswith ".py" and InitiatingProcessFileName !endswith "python.exe"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Examine the initiating process — extract its SHA256, signing status, and parent process. Cross-check against known cloud SDKs (python's dropbox module, Go SDK clients). RokRAT/BirdCall typically run as unsigned C++ binaries with random/temp paths. Step 2 (contain): If the process is unsigned and runs from %APPDATA%, %TEMP%, %PROGRAMDATA%, or a sqgame folder — isolate and quarantine. Block the suspicious process hash org-wide. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the process's parent chain looking for Ruby/Python loader execution (BirdCall's documented multistage loader); search HKCU\\Run and Scheduled Tasks for persistence written by the same process; sweep for additional hosts where the same unsigned binary contacted Dropbox/pCloud.
let CloudC2 = dynamic(["api.dropboxapi.com","content.dropboxapi.com","api.pcloud.com","eapi.pcloud.com","api.pcloud.link"]);
let KnownClients = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Dropbox.exe","DropboxUpdate.exe","pCloud.exe","OneDrive.exe","explorer.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (CloudC2) or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) has_any (CloudC2)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownClients)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize EventCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Urls=make_set(RemoteUrl,10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where EventCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let CloudC2 = dynamic(["api.dropboxapi.com","content.dropboxapi.com","api.pcloud.com","eapi.pcloud.com","api.pcloud.link"]);
let KnownClients = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Dropbox.exe","DropboxUpdate.exe","pCloud.exe","OneDrive.exe","explorer.exe"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (ImNetworkSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
     | where DstHostname has_any (CloudC2) or Url has_any (CloudC2)
     | where ProcessName !in~ (KnownClients)
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Process=ProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Dst=coalesce(DstHostname,Url), Src="ImNetworkSession"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
     | where DestinationHostName has_any (CloudC2) or RequestURL has_any (CloudC2)
     | where isnotempty(SourceHostName)
     | extend Process = tostring(split(DeviceCustomString1, "|")[0])
     | where Process !in~ (KnownClients) or isempty(Process)
     | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, User=SourceUserName, Process, Cmd=RequestURL, Dst=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Src="CommonSecurityLog"))
| summarize EventCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Destinations=make_set(Dst,10) by Host, Process, User
| where EventCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*dropboxapi.com OR *api.pcloud.com OR *eapi.pcloud.com OR *api.pcloud.link) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\Dropbox.exe OR *\\pCloud.exe OR *\\OneDrive.exe OR *\\explorer.exe)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(dropboxapi\.com|api\.pcloud\.com|eapi\.pcloud\.com|api\.pcloud\.link)$/i
| ContextImageFileName!=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|Dropbox|DropboxUpdate|pCloud|OneDrive|explorer)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

DeviceProcessEvents

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or SHA1 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or MD5 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or SHA1 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9") or MD5 in~ ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:

tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("03E3ECE9F48CF4104AAFC535790CA2FB3C6B26CF", "FC0C691DB7E2D2BD3B0B4C1E24D18DF72168B7D9")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]

Shai-Hulud npm preinstall: node spawns Bun runtime from bun-dl-* tmpdir AIInstallation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's signature execution chain where the malicious npm preinstall hook (node setup.mjs) downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime to a mkdtempSync-created directory prefixed bun-dl- and then executes execution.js under Bun to evade EDRs that only watch for node children of npm install. Targets the exact loader behaviour in setup.mjs (SHA256 4066781f...) shared across mbt@1.2.48 and the three compromised @cap-js packages. Rationale: Pivots on the exact mkdtempSync prefix 'bun-dl-' and the platform-specific Bun release-asset names (bun-windows-x64-baseline, bun-linux-x64-baseline, bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline, bun-linux-aarch64, bun-darwin) hard-coded in setup.mjs (SHA256 4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34), plus the literal 'execution.js' filename — the article calls out 'a different binary name that bypasses' EDR monitors of node children, which is the exact behaviour this UC flips back into a detection. IOCs taken directly from StepSecurity's runtime trace.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where (FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
      or FolderPath has "bun-dl-"
      or FolderPath has "bun-windows-x64-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-x64-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline"
      or FolderPath has "bun-linux-aarch64"
      or FolderPath has "bun-darwin"
      or ProcessCommandLine has "execution.js")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","preinstall","npm install","yarn install","pnpm install")
   or FolderPath has "bun-dl-"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun-dl-","bun-windows-x64-baseline","bun-linux-x64-baseline","bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline","bun-linux-aarch64","bun-darwin","execution.js")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","preinstall","npm install","yarn install","pnpm install")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has "bun-dl-"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shai-Hulud AI coding-agent persistence: .claude/settings.json + .vscode/tasks.json drops AIInstallation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's novel persistence mechanism where the payload commits or writes .claude/settings.json (abusing Claude Code's SessionStart hook) and .vscode/tasks.json (with runOn:folderOpen) into every accessible repository. Any developer re-opening the repo in VSCode or Claude Code silently re-executes the malware — this is one of the first supply-chain campaigns weaponising AI-agent config files. Rationale: The article describes 'one of the first supply chain attacks to target AI coding agent configurations as a persistence and propagation vector', specifically dropping .claude/settings.json (SessionStart hook abuse) and .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen. Detection bucket-aggregates both filenames in a 1h window because the loader writes them as a pair, and falls back to the suspect-parent process list (node/bun/git) when only one of the two files is observed — that combination is essentially nil in legitimate developer activity. Sigma omitted because the detection is a multi-file correlation, not a single event.
ATT&CKT1546 T1195.002 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let _window = 1h;
let _suspect_files = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where (FolderPath endswith @"\.claude\settings.json"
          or FolderPath endswith "/.claude/settings.json"
          or FolderPath endswith @"\.vscode\tasks.json"
          or FolderPath endswith "/.vscode/tasks.json")
    | extend FileKind = case(
        FolderPath has ".claude", "claude_settings",
        FolderPath has ".vscode", "vscode_tasks",
        "other")
    | extend Bucket = bin(Timestamp, _window);
_suspect_files
| summarize FilesDropped = make_set(FileKind),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Paths = make_set(FolderPath, 50),
            Initiators = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 20),
            InitiatingCmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 20)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Bucket
| where array_length(FilesDropped) >= 2
   or Initiators has_any ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","git.exe","git")
| order by FirstSeen desc
let _window = 1h;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath endswith @"\.claude\settings.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith "/.claude/settings.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith @"\.vscode\tasks.json"
      or TargetFilePath endswith "/.vscode/tasks.json")
| extend FileKind = case(
    TargetFilePath has ".claude", "claude_settings",
    TargetFilePath has ".vscode", "vscode_tasks",
    "other")
| extend Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, _window)
| summarize FilesDropped = make_set(FileKind),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50),
            Actors = make_set(ActorUsername, 20),
            ActingProcs = make_set(ActingProcessName, 20),
            ActingCmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 20)
            by DvcHostname, Bucket
| where array_length(FilesDropped) >= 2
   or ActingProcs has_any ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","git.exe","git")
| order by FirstSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\.claude\\settings.json OR */.claude/settings.json OR *\\.vscode\\tasks.json OR */.vscode/tasks.json) OR @file.path:(*\\.claude\\settings.json OR */.claude/settings.json OR *\\.vscode\\tasks.json OR */.vscode/tasks.json)) (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\git.exe OR */node OR */bun OR */git) OR @process.executable.path:(*\\node.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\git.exe OR */node OR */bun OR */git))
ENDPOINT

Shai-Hulud known-bad setup.mjs / execution.js SHA256 hash match AIInstallation High
Detects on-disk or in-execution presence of the two Shai-Hulud loader/payload files by their byte-identical SHA256 hashes — the setup.mjs loader (4066781f...) is identical across all four confirmed compromised packages (mbt@1.2.48, @cap-js/sqlite@2.2.2, @cap-js/postgres@v2.2.2, @cap-js/db-service@v2.10.1), and execution.js (80a3d287...) is the 11.6 MB obfuscated credential stealer. This is the highest-fidelity retrospective hunt across npm-using hosts and CI runners. Rationale: The article explicitly states setup.mjs is 'SHA-256 (identical across all compromised packages) 4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34' and execution.js for mbt@1.2.48 is 80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac. These are the highest-fidelity IOCs in the campaign — byte-identical across four packages confirms the same operator/toolchain. Union across file, process and image-load tables ensures retrospective coverage whether the artifact landed on disk only, was executed, or was loaded.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let _ShaiHulud_Hashes = dynamic([
    "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",  // setup.mjs (loader, identical across all 4 compromised packages)
    "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac"   // execution.js (11.6MB obfuscated payload from mbt@1.2.48)
]);
union isfuzzy=true
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ProcessCreated", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, Source="DeviceProcessEvents" ),
    ( DeviceImageLoadEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ImageLoaded", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine="",
                  InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc
let _ShaiHulud_Hashes = dynamic([
    "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",
    "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac"
]);
union isfuzzy=true
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes) or Hash in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath,
                  Hash = coalesce(TargetFileSHA256, Hash), ActingProcessName, ActorUsername,
                  Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where SHA256 in (_ShaiHulud_Hashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType="ProcessCreated",
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  Hash = SHA256, ActingProcessName = ParentProcessName,
                  ActorUsername, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,

// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application

status: experimental
description: |

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (

    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication

      AND Authentication.signature IN (

    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
